name: CA-36
label: Safe D

key_factors: Deep-blue D+21 district with a well-established incumbent
Overwhelming fundraising gap: Lieu $1.8M raised vs. Brignano ~$5K
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97%
No public polls or expert ratings; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Ted Lieu combines a heavily Democratic electorate, incumbency, and a massive money advantage against a challenger who has raised almost nothing, and markets price his win at 97 percent. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, this stays solidly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any sign of unexpected challenger funding or a sharply altered turnout environment would be the main thing that could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ted Lieu, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Los Angeles-area district with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward Democrats. He advanced to the general election and faces Republican Houston Brignano, a first-time challenger with minimal financial backing. Lieu has raised roughly $1.8 million and holds about $1.2 million on hand, along with modest outside support, while Brignano has raised about $5,000.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the stark money gap. Prediction markets put Lieu's chances of winning at about 97 percent. The combination of a deep-blue electorate, a well-funded incumbent, and an under-resourced opponent makes this seat solidly Democratic heading into the general election, with little evidence pointing to a competitive contest.
